title: SLO Launch Field Kit and Ops Liaison Rotations
content:
Purpose and scope:

This is a compact field kit for launching service-level objectives (SLOs) across teams and for establishing a temporary ops liaison rotation to smooth the first 60–90 days of a rollout. Focus is cross-functional: product/feature teams, platform, SRE, and solutions eng. Use this doc as a checklist + working notes during the pilot phase of any new SLO or major SLO change.

Why this is needed (problem statement):
- SLO launches often stall because operational responsibilities are not clear in the first weeks; telemetry thresholds, alerts, and stakeholder triggers are misaligned.
- Early false positives and noisy alerts erode trust; teams revert or mute signals before the SLO has time to stabilize.
- There is no lightweight, repeatable rotation pattern for platform to support feature teams during the critical onramp.

High-level goals (success criteria):
1) First 30 days: no critical outages caused by misconfigured SLO alerts and a documented runbook for common alarms.
2) 60 days: measured signal quality (false positive rate < 20% for new alerts) and adoption of at least one mitigation automation (auto-scaling, fallback routing, or pre-warm).
3) 90 days: handoff complete, liaison exits rotation, and SLO is owned by product + SRE with an agreed cadence for review.

Who should be involved (roles & responsibilities):
- Feature/Product Owner: defines customer-facing intent, key user journeys, and impact matrix.
- SRE Lead (onboarded): owns alert tuning, runbook creation, and postmortem process.
- Platform Engineer Liaison (rotation): provides immediate help on routing, capacity and config; bridges to infra teams.
- Observability Engineer: sets up telemetry, dashboards, and synthetic probes.
- Solutions/SE contact: validates customer-facing behavior and rollout comms.
- QA / Perf: runs spike tests and validates thresholds under load.

Ops liaison rotation pattern (recommended):
- Length: 2-week stints for each liaison, 8–12 weeks total support window for a typical SLO launch.
- Roster: platform-engineering contributors + 1 SRE buddy per sprint. Minimum overlap: 3 days handoff between liaisons.
- On-call parity: liaisons should not replace primary oncall but act as subject-matter responders for SLO-specific signals.
- Deliverables per liaison period: updated runbook section, 1 tuning pass on alerts, one dashboard iteration, and a documented de-noising action (e.g., metric filter, composite alert).

Launch checklist (pre-launch, day 0, week 1–4, week 5–12):
A) Pre-launch (2–4 weeks before):
- Confirm intent doc and customer journeys (owner: Product).
- Define measurable SLOs, indicators (SLIs), and error budgets (owner: SRE + Product).
- Create initial dashboards and synthetic checks (owner: Observability).
- Draft runbook template with triage steps and tests to reproduce (owner: Feature + SRE).
- Map linked artifacts (Jira tickets, PRs, Confluence pages) and communication list.
- Identify liaison roster and confirm rotation schedule.

B) Day 0 (go-live):
- Smoke test synthetic checks and baseline dashboards.
- Turn on alerts in quiet mode (notify-only) for 24–48 hours if possible.
- Liaison kickoff sync (15–30m): align handoff, urgent contacts, quick war-room plan.

C) Week 1–2 (stabilize):
- Triage initial alerts, categorize noise vs real incidents.
- Runbook iteration 1: codify observed triage patterns.
- Quick perf stress: run narrow spike tests during low-traffic window.
- Postmortem-lite for any incidents (owner: SRE + Feature).

D) Week 3–4 (de-noise):
- Tune alert thresholds and apply suppression windows where appropriate.
- Instrument additional SLIs if gaps are identified.
- Begin scheduling regular SLO review slots (biweekly for first 8 weeks).

E) Week 5–12 (handoff & automation):
- Implement at least one automation (auto-scaling profile, warm pool, or fallback).
- Validate that false positive rate trends downward and alert precision improves.
- Formal handoff doc completed and accepted by SRE + Product.
- Liaison rotation concludes once ownership sign-off is obtained.

Key artifacts and templates (starter snippets to copy):
- Runbook template: Summary, who to page, triage steps, mitigations, escalation, reversion plan, postmortem link.
- Tuning log: timestamped entries of alert parameter changes and rationale.
- Signal health spreadsheet: counts of alerts, incidents, false positives, mean time to acknowledge, mean time to mitigate.
- Handoff acceptance checklist: runbook complete, dashboards stable, automation validated, errors within agreed budget.

Signal quality metrics to track (minimum set):
- Alert volume / day (broken down by severity).
- False positive rate (manual classification during liaison period).
- Time to acknowledge (TTA) and time to mitigate (TTM).
- Error budget consumption trajectory (7-day and 30-day).
- User-facing impact incidents (severity >= P2) during onramp.

Common early risks and mitigations: 
- Risk: Noisy client-side retries inflate error rate. Mitigation: add client-side dedupe or sampling, instrumented counts for retries.
- Risk: Misaligned aggregation windows causing spike sensitivity. Mitigation: align SLI windows with user-visible latency patterns; test with synthetic traffic.
- Risk: Runbook absent or incomplete. Mitigation: liaison must publish a minimally viable runbook in first 72 hours.

Communication plan (who/when/how):
- Pre-launch email to stakeholders summarizing intent and schedule.
- Day 0 status Slack channel with pinned runbook and contacts.
- Weekly short “signal health” bulletin during liaison rotation (2–3 bullet summary).
- Post-launch retrospective at day 30 and day 90.

Decision gates for rollback or pause:
- If error budget consumption > 50% within first 7 days and user-impacting incidents occur -> pause rollout and invoke rollback plan.
- If alert false positive rate > 50% after week 2 -> escalate to SRE lead and schedule immediate tuning block.

Handoff acceptance criteria (to exit liaison rotation):
- Runbook passes checklist and is accessible to the oncall team.
- False positives reduced to under 20% for key alerts or clear mitigation path documented.
- Observability baseline established (synthetics, dashboards, and alerting stable for 7 consecutive days).
- Product and SRE sign off on continued cadence and review frequency.

Quick templates (copy into a new doc):
- Liaison handoff note: dates, current open actions, known flakes, critical dashboards, next steps.
- Runbook snippet: Immediate mitigation -> Scale up warm pool; If warm pool insufficient -> reroute traffic to fallback model; If user-impacting -> page SRE lead.

Open questions / decisions pending (working):
1) Do we require all SLO launches to run liaison rotations by policy, or keep as recommended? (proposal: recommended for first 3 months after rollout)
2) What is the minimal data retention for signal tuning logs? (proposal: 90 days)
3) Who owns the liaison roster and backfill commitments across holidays? (proposal: platform-engineering to maintain primary roster, SRE to provide secondary coverage)

Next steps (immediate owner assignments):
- Evelyn (owner): finalize roster and publish calendar invites for next pilot (by 2026-05-18).
- Diego (Observability): create the synthetic checks template and baseline dashboard (by 2026-05-20).
- Priya (SRE): draft runbook template and postmortem-lite checklist (by 2026-05-21).

Notes to self / tacit knowledge:
- Keep liaison tasks lightweight — do the minimal set of changes that restore signal fidelity without overengineering.
- Communicate progress with short bullets; engineers stop reading long prose during active incidents.
- Preserve a short tuning history for auditability; teams will ask why thresholds moved.

If you use this kit: copy the runbook template, fill the liaison roster, and reach out in #platform-slo-onramp with questions or to request help.

Document history: initial draft 2026-05-12 by Evelyn Park; liaison pattern suggestions and checklist edits added 2026-06-03 by Diego Ramos and Priya Nair.
